title: Electromagnetic Induction
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: Magnetic Flux Φ: Definition, formula, SI unit, and dimensions?
cards.a:
Φ = B · A = B A cos θ, where θ is angle between magnetic field B and normal to area vector A.
SI unit: Weber (Wb) = Tesla·m² (T·m²). CGS unit: Maxwell (1 Wb = 10⁸ Maxwell).
Dimensions: [M¹ L² T⁻² I⁻¹].
cards.hint: Scalar quantity. Φ is maximum when field B is normal to plane of surface (θ = 0°).

cards.q: State Faraday's Laws of Electromagnetic Induction.
cards.a:
First Law: Whenever magnetic flux linked with a closed circuit changes, an induced EMF is set up in the circuit which lasts as long as the change in flux continues.
Second Law: The magnitude of induced EMF is directly proportional to the time rate of change of magnetic flux: e ∝ dΦ/dt.
cards.hint: Mathematical form with Lenz's law: e = - N (dΦ / dt).

cards.q: State Lenz's Law and its fundamental conservation basis.
cards.a:
The direction of induced current is always such that it OPPOSES the very cause (change in magnetic flux) that produces it: e = - dΦ / dt.
Conservation basis: Law of Conservation of ENERGY.
cards.hint: Mechanical work done against opposing magnetic forces is converted directly into electrical energy.

cards.q: Induced EMF, Induced Current, and Total Induced Charge in a circuit of resistance R?
cards.a:
Induced EMF: e = - dΦ / dt
Induced Current: I = e / R = - (1 / R) (dΦ / dt)
Total Induced Charge: q = ∫ I dt = ΔΦ / R.
cards.hint: Crucial distinction: Induced EMF and current depend on the RATE of change of flux (how fast), but total induced charge q depends ONLY on total change in flux ΔΦ, independent of time taken!

cards.q: Motional EMF induced in a conductor of length L moving with velocity v perpendicular to field B?
cards.a:
e = B L v.
If angle between v and B is θ: e = B L v sin θ.
Direction of induced current: Given by Fleming's Right-Hand Rule.
cards.hint: Vector form: e = ∮ (v × B) · dl.

cards.q: Induced EMF in a conducting rod of length L rotating with angular speed ω about one end in a perpendicular magnetic field B?
cards.a: e = (1/2) B L² ω = B A f, where A = π L² is area swept per revolution and f = ω / 2π is frequency.
cards.hint: Frequent Board numerical! Effective speed is average speed of midpoint: v_avg = ω L / 2 ⇒ e = B L (ω L / 2) = (1/2) B L² ω.

cards.q: What are Eddy Currents (Foucault Currents) and how are they minimized?
cards.a:
Circulating loop currents induced in bulk metallic conductors when magnetic flux through them changes.
Minimization: Using laminated cores (thin metal sheets separated by insulating varnish layer) instead of solid metal blocks.
cards.hint: Applications: Induction furnace, electromagnetic braking in high-speed trains, dead-beat galvanometers, induction cooktops.

cards.q: Self-Induction: Definition, formula, SI unit, and dimensions of Self-Inductance L?
cards.a:
Production of induced EMF in a coil due to change of current in the same coil: Φ = L I ⇒ e = - L (dI / dt).
Self-inductance: L = |e| / (dI / dt). SI unit: Henry (H) = Wb/A = V·s/A.
Dimensions: [M¹ L² T⁻² I⁻²].
cards.hint: Self-inductance represents 'electrical inertia' (analogous to mass in mechanics), opposing any change in current.

cards.q: Self-inductance L of a long solenoid of length l, area A, and N total turns?
cards.a: L = μ₀ n² A l = μ₀ (N² / l) A = μ₀ μ_r N² A / l (with iron core of relative permeability μ_r).
cards.hint: Notice L ∝ N² (proportional to the SQUARE of number of turns!). Doubling turns quadruples inductance.

cards.q: Energy stored in a current-carrying Inductor and Magnetic Energy Density?
cards.a:
Stored Energy: U = (1/2) L I².
Magnetic Energy Density (energy per unit volume of magnetic field): u_B = B² / (2 μ₀).
cards.hint: Exact magnetic counterpart of capacitor energy U = (1/2) C V² and electric energy density u_E = (1/2) ε₀ E².

cards.q: Mutual Induction: Definition, formula, and Coefficient of Coupling K?
cards.a:
Production of induced EMF in secondary coil due to change of current in primary coil: Φ₂ = M I₁ ⇒ e₂ = - M (dI₁ / dt).
Mutual Inductance of two coaxial solenoids: M = μ₀ n₁ n₂ A l = (μ₀ N₁ N₂ A) / l.
Coefficient of Coupling: K = M / √(L₁ L₂), where 0 ≤ K ≤ 1.
cards.hint: K = 1 for tightly coupled coils (100% flux linkage); K = 0 for perpendicular coils with zero mutual flux.

cards.q: Combination of Inductors: Series and Parallel formulas?
cards.a:
Series (no mutual induction): L_s = L₁ + L₂.
Series assisting: L_s = L₁ + L₂ + 2 M; Series opposing: L_s = L₁ + L₂ - 2 M.
Parallel (no mutual induction): 1 / L_p = 1 / L₁ + 1 / L₂ ⇒ L_p = (L₁ L₂) / (L₁ + L₂).
cards.hint: Inductors combine mathematically exactly like electrical resistors.

cards.q: AC Generator: Working equation of generated alternating EMF?
cards.a: e = e₀ sin(ω t) = N B A ω sin(ω t), where peak EMF is e₀ = N B A ω = 2 π f N B A.
cards.hint: EMF is maximum (e = e₀) when plane of coil is PARALLEL to magnetic field (flux Φ = 0, but dΦ/dt is maximum!).

cards.q: A copper ring is dropped horizontally through a vertical bar magnet. What is its acceleration compared to g?
cards.a:
Acceleration is strictly LESS than g (a < g) while entering AND while leaving the magnet!
By Lenz's law, the induced current creates an opposing upward magnetic force retarding the fall.
cards.hint: If the copper ring has a cut/gap, no continuous current flows, and it falls freely with a = g!

cards.q: Transformer: Principle, construction, and transformation ratio k?
cards.a:
Principle: Mutual Induction between two coils on a common laminated iron core. Operates strictly on AC (never on DC!).
Transformation ratio: k = e_s / e_p = N_s / N_p = I_p / I_s.
cards.hint: For an ideal transformer, input power = output power (e_p I_p = e_s I_s).

cards.q: Step-Up vs Step-Down Transformer: Characteristics?
cards.a:
Step-Up (k > 1): N_s > N_p ⇒ e_s > e_p (voltage increases), but I_s < I_p (current decreases).
Step-Down (k < 1): N_s < N_p ⇒ e_s < e_p (voltage decreases), but I_s > I_p (current increases).
cards.hint: A transformer changes voltage and current levels, but NEVER changes power or frequency (f_out = f_in)!

cards.q: Energy losses in a practical Transformer and how to minimize them?
cards.a:
1. Copper loss (I²R in windings): Use thick copper wires.
2. Eddy current loss (iron core heating): Use laminated soft iron core.
3. Hysteresis loss: Use high-permeability soft iron with narrow hysteresis loop.
4. Flux leakage: Wind primary and secondary coils coaxially one over the other.
cards.hint: Board 3-mark theory question! Efficiency is η = Output Power / Input Power = (e_s I_s) / (e_p I_p).

cards.q: Growth and Decay of current in an L-R circuit: Time constant τ?
cards.a:
Inductive Time Constant: τ = L / R (SI unit: seconds).
Growth: I(t) = I₀ [ 1 - e^(-t / τ) ], where at t = τ, I = 0.632 I₀ (63.2% of maximum).
Decay: I(t) = I₀ · e^(-t / τ), where at t = τ, current falls to 0.368 I₀ (36.8%).
cards.hint: Dimensions of L/R are identical to time: [M⁰ L⁰ T¹].

cards.q: What happens if a steady DC voltage V is applied across an inductor of resistance R?
cards.a:
At t = 0 (just after closing switch): Inductor offers INFINITE resistance (acts as an OPEN CIRCUIT, I = 0).
At t = ∞ (steady state): Inductor offers ZERO resistance (acts as an ideal SHORT CIRCUIT, I = V / R).
cards.hint: Opposite to a capacitor! (A capacitor is short at t=0, open at t=∞).

cards.q: Back EMF in a DC Motor: Formula and mechanical power output?
cards.a:
Induced back EMF: e = V - I R_a (where R_a is armature resistance).
Mechanical Power: P_mech = e · I = V I - I² R_a.
Efficiency: η = e / V.
cards.hint: Mechanical power output is maximum when back EMF is exactly half of supply voltage: e = V / 2.

cards.q: What is Non-conservative nature of Induced Electric Field?
cards.a:
A changing magnetic field induces an electric field whose line integral around a closed loop is NON-ZERO: ∮ E · dl = - dΦ / dt ≠ 0.
This induced electric field is non-electrostatic and non-conservative (cannot be defined by a scalar potential).
cards.hint: Field lines of induced electric field form continuous closed loops without sources or sinks.

cards.q: External force and power required to pull a conducting rod of length L with velocity v in field B?
cards.a:
Force: F = B I L = (B² L² v) / R
Power: P = F · v = (B² L² v²) / R = I² R.
cards.hint: Mechanical power input equals rate of Joule heat dissipation in the circuit (energy conservation).

cards.q: If a coil of N turns, area A, and resistance R is flipped by 180° in uniform field B, what is the charge flown?
cards.a:
Initial flux: Φ₁ = N B A; Final flux: Φ₂ = - N B A.
ΔΦ = 2 N B A.
Charge flown: q = ΔΦ / R = 2 N B A / R.
cards.hint: Flipping by 180° always doubles the flux change (ΔΦ = 2 NBA).

cards.q: Self-inductance of a circular coil of radius R and N turns?
cards.a: L = (μ₀ π N² R) / 2.
cards.hint: Derived from L = N Φ / I = N (B · A) / I with B_center = μ₀ N I / (2 R).

cards.q: MHT-CET Trap: A DC source of 12 V is connected across primary of a step-up transformer (N_s/N_p = 10). What is the output voltage at secondary?
cards.a:
Output voltage is ZERO (0 V)!
A transformer works strictly on CHANGING flux (AC). A constant DC voltage produces zero rate of change of flux (dΦ/dt = 0), so induced secondary EMF is zero.
cards.hint: Connecting DC to a transformer core may also burn out the primary winding due to lack of back EMF!
